dropped.reason: (b) Warm-up artifact. cross_ema(A^3, 241) with A = X^3 / sum of X^3 over the last 241 days. A is exactly 1 on each stock's first valid day (x/x), then decays roughly as 1/d. Cubed, those first days are about 1 in size, while genuine volume spikes give A^3 of only 1e-5 to 1e-2, and the 241-day half-life keeps the first days' weight for years. In a synthetic simulation, 94-99% of the value over 4 years came from the first 60 days after the first bar, with rank correlation 0.87-0.98 to that part. So the cross-sectional ranking reflects the date of the stock's first bar (listing age, data start, long suspensions) plus its early volume path, not the intended volume-burstiness mechanism. Its 0.31 correlation with market cap also fits a recent-IPO tilt.
